Name: Interpersonal Skills
Description: Shows understanding, friendliness, courtesy, tact, empathy, concern, and politeness to others; develops and maintains effective relationships with others; may include effectively dealing with individuals who are difficult, hostile, or distressed; relates well to people from varied backgrounds and different situations; is sensitive to cultural diversity, race, gender, disabilities, and other individual differences.

Name: Accountability
Description: Holds self and others accountable for measurable high-quality, timely, and cost-effective results. Determines objectives, sets priorities, and delegates work. Accepts responsibility for mistakes. Complies with established control systems and rules.

Name: Conflict Management
Description: Manages and resolves conflicts, grievances, confrontations, or disagreements in a constructive manner to minimize negative personal impact.

Name: Continual Learning
Description: Assesses and recognizes own strengths and weaknesses; pursues self-developmen

Name: Decisiveness
Description: Makes well-informed, effective, and timely decisions, even when data are limited or solutions produce unpleasant consequences; perceives the impact and implications of decisions.

Name: Flexibility
Description: Is open to change and new information; adapts behavior or work methods in response to new information, changing conditions, or unexpected obstacles; effectively deals with ambiguity.

Name: Managing Human Resources
Description: Plans, distributes, coordinates, and monitors work assignments of others; evaluates work performance and provides feedback to others on their performance; ensures that staff are appropriately selected, utilized, and developed, and that they are treated in a fair and equitable manner.

Name: Influencing
Description: Persuades others to accept recommendations, cooperate, or change their behavior; works with others towards an agreement; negotiates to find mutually acceptable solutions.

Name: Integrity / Honesty
Description: Contributes to maintaining the integrity of the organization; displays high standards of ethical conduct and understands the impact of violating these standards on an organization, self, and others; is trustworthy.

Name: Public Service Motivation
Description: Shows a commitment to serve the public. Ensures that actions meet public needs; aligns organizational objectives and practices with public interests.

Name: Negotiating
Description: Works with others towards an agreement that may involve exchanging specific resources or resolving differences.

Name: Oral Communication
Description: Expresses information (for example, ideas or facts) to individuals or groups effectively, taking into account the audience and nature of the information (for example, technical, sensitive, controversial); makes clear and convincing oral presentations; listens to others, attends to nonverbal cues, and responds appropriately.

Name: Problem Solving
Description: Identifies problems; determines accuracy and relevance of information; uses sound judgment to generate and evaluate alternatives, and to make recommendations

Name: Resilience
Description: Deals effectively with pressure; remains optimistic and persistent, even under adversity. Recovers quickly from setbacks.

Name: Strategic Thinking
Description: Formulates objectives and priorities, and implements plans consistent with the long-term interests of the organization in a global environment. Capitalizes on opportunities and manages risks.

Name: Team Building
Description: Inspires and fosters team commitment, spirit, pride, and trust. Facilitates cooperation and motivates team members to accomplish group goals.

Name: Written Communication
Description: Writes in a clear, concise, organized, and convincing manner for the intended audience.

Name: Administration and Management
Description: Assimilates information; applies agency policies and procedures; delegates authority and makes decisions; assesses and uses available resources to complete agency programs.

Name: Attention To Detail
Description: Performs thorough and detailed work and is conscientious about attending to detail.

Name: Information Management
Description: Identifies a need for and knows where or how to gather information; organizes and maintains information or information management systems.

Name: Mathematical Reasoning
Description: Solves practical problems by choosing appropriately from a variety of mathematical, statistical, and financial techniques.

Name: Mathematics
Description: Performs computations such as addition, subtraction, multiplication, and division correctly using whole numbers, fractions, decimals, and percentages.

Name: Memory
Description: Retains and recalls information.

Name: Organizational Awareness
Description: Understands the organization’s mission and functions; operates effectively within the social, political, and technological systems including the programs, rules, policies, procedures, and regulations of the organization.

Name: Reasoning
Description: Interprets rules, principles, or relationships that explain facts, data, or other information; analyzes information and reviews alternatives in order to draw accurate conclusions.

Name: Teaching Others
Description: Helps others learn through formal or informal methods; identifies training needs; provides constructive feedback; coaches others on how to perform tasks; acts as a mentor.

Name: Business Law
Description: Knowledge of business and commercial law, including the Uniform Commercial Code (UCC) and contract law, as they pertain to credit unions.

Name: Corporate Governance
Description: Knowledge of generally accepted industry standards and protocols for due diligence; including internal controls, control structure/environment, director and management accountability, fiduciary responsibility, reporting structures, and management oversight.

Name: Economics
Description: Knowledge of relevant economic issues, financial markets, and financial institutions.

Name: Marketing
Description: Knowledge of tools and techniques (e.g., demographics, data aggregation, penetration, member relationship management) for promoting products, services, and programs.

Name: Organizational Structure
Description: Knowledge of credit union organizational structures (e.g., accountability, communication channels, work flow, delineation of responsibility, supervisory relationships, organizational chart) and general legal structures (e.g., CUSOs).

Name: Risk Management
Description: Knowledge of methods and tools used for enterprise-wide risk management (i.e. integrating assessments of risk across the credit union to determine and mitigate overall risk exposure).

Name: Statistics
Description: Knowledge of statistical principles, methods, and tools; ability to use statistical data in order to make recommendations or decisions.

Name: Strategic Management
Description: Knowledge of the fundamental aspects of the planning process.  Ability to analyze relationships between strategic and business plans and their impact on the credit union’s financial condition, operations, or reputation.

Name: Prioritization
Description: Ability to determine and prioritize areas to be reviewed during an examination or supervision contact.

Name: Credit Administration
Description: Knowledge of lending principles, industry practices, and markets; including policies, underwriting and documentation, pricing, purchasing, selling, servicing, and collecting consumer, real estate, commercial loans, and participation loans.

Name: Examination Techniques and Procedures
Description: Knowledge of examination procedures; ability to analyze information to identify and determine appropriate actions needed to resolve concerns.

Name: Financial Analysis
Description: Knowledge of the fundamentals of business finance, financial analysis, and asset-liability management (ALM) including internal and external sources of funding; ability to analyze and interpret financial trends and ratios, assess current financial conditions and projections.

Name: Management Information Systems
Description: Knowledge of the structure of electronic processing systems, information security, third party reviews, and disaster recovery, including electronic payment systems (e.g., web-based FedLine, electronic data processing (EDP), Internet).

Name: Regulatory Environment
Description: Knowledge of federal, state, and local laws and regulations affecting credit unions (e.g., Federal Credit Union Act, NCUA Rules and Regulations, Bank Secrecy Act, Bylaws, consumer compliance regulations).

Name: Accounting
Description: Knowledge of financial reporting, accounting theory and concepts covered by generally accepted accounting principles (GAAP), with an emphasis on financial institutions; knowledge of accounting systems, structures, and controls; ability to evaluate financial statements and other financial records.

Name: Auditing
Description: Knowledge of generally accepted auditing standards (GAAS) and procedures for financial and compliance audits; ability to understand the concepts of internal controls, substantive testing, and the auditor's report.

Name: Internal Controls
Description: Knowledge of internal control structure and components that maintain integrity of financial and compliance reporting activities; ability to evaluate the credit union’s risk of material misstatement and compliace violations due to internal control deficiencies.

Name: Fraud
Description: Knowledge of types of fraud, indicators of possible fraud, and techniques to identify, investigate, and document fraud.

Name: Policy Knowledge Maintenance
Description: Maintains and builds on policy knowledge to stay abreast of changes and updates to internal Agency policy and relevant external policies.

Name: Credit Risk Management
Description: Knowledge of methods and tools used for credit risk management; ability to assess risk across the loan portfolio , including credit risk management practices and processes, allowance methodologies, collections, and workouts; ability to identify and evaluate mitigants for aggregate portfolio risk.

Name: Business Loans
Description: Knowledge of regulations and guidance, lending principles, industry practices, and markets related to business loans; ability to assess risks and risk management practices associated with individual business loans and the aggregate portfolio.

Name: Residential Mortgage Loans
Description: Knowledge of regulations and guidance, lending principles, and industry practices related to residential mortgage loans; ability to assess risks and risk management practices associated with mortgage loans.

Name: Indirect Loans/Leases
Description: Knowledge of regulations and guidance, lending principles, and industry practices related to indirect loans/leases; ability to assess risks and risk management practices associated with indirect loans/leases.

Name: Investments
Description: Knowledge of investment policies and principles, industry practices, and markets, including pre-purchase analysis, portfolio management, permissible investment activities, characteristics (e.g., cash flows, indices, pricing, optionality), and related risk.

Name: Liquidity Risk Management
Description: Knowledge of regulations and supervisory guidance related to liquidity risk and methods to identify, measure, monitor, and control liquidity risk; ability to assess liquidity risk, including actions to mitigate liquidity risk.

Name: Interest Rate Risk Management
Description: Knowledge of regulations and supervisory guidance related to interest rate risk and methods to identify, measure, monitor, and control interest rate risk; ability to assess interest rate risk, including actions to mitigate interest rate risk.

Name: Asset Liability Management Modeling
Description: Knowledge of models used to estimate the financial risks to which the institution is exposed; ability to assess adequacy of the credit union’s asset liability management (ALM) models and practices.

Name: Compliance Risk Management
Description: Knowledge of the laws, regulations, and supervisory guidance related to compliance risk and methods to identify, measure, monitor, and control compliance risk; ability to assess compliance risk, including actions to mitigate compliance risk; ability to facilitate resolution when violations occur.

Name: Federal Consumer Protection Laws and Regulations
Description: Knowledge of federal consumer protection laws and regulations applicable to credit unions (for example, Truth in Savings Act, Regulations B, C, D, E, M, P, X, Z), including consequences of non-compliance; ability to determine compliance with laws and regulations.

Name: Payment System Infrastructure
Description: Knowledge of payment system delivery channels, components, and structure; ability to assess payment systems and related risk, including actions to mitigate risk.

Name: Payment System Oversight
Description: Knowledge of standards, processes, and practices to identify, measure, prevent, and mitigate risks, threats, and vulnerabilities associated with payment systems.

Name: Payment System Governance
Description: Knowledge of NCUA Rules and Regulations, agency directives and guidance, and  industry rules, guidelines, and best practices related to identifying, measuring, managing, monitoring, reporting, and controlling risks in payment systems; ability to assess governance and related risks.

Name: Payment System Security and Controls
Description: Knowledge of logical and physical access controls and oversight activities used to ensure protection of credit union assets and integrity of payment information (e.g., member information, PII).

Name: Information Technology Governance
Description: Knowledge of NCUA rules and regulations (e.g., RR Part 748, 749), agency directives and guidance, and industry best practices related to managing, monitoring, reporting, and controlling risks in information technology; ability to assess governance and related risks.

Name: Information Technology Risk Management
Description: Knowledge of standards, tools, and practices to identify, detect, prevent, and mitigate information technology risks, threats, and vulnerabilities; includes the risk assessment process, risk management program, and the audit function; ability to assess adequacy of controls.

Name: Information Security Controls
Description: Knowledge of logical and physical tools and techniques to ensure protection, confidentiality, integrity, and availability of data and information.

Name: Business Continuity
Description: Knowledge of policies, procedures, and practices (e.g., business impact analysis, risk management, testing) to ensure continuity of business operations in the event of a disaster or incident.

Name: BSA/AML Compliance Risk Management
Description: Knowledge of BSA/AML laws, rules, regulations, and supervisory guidance and the methods to identify, measure, monitor, and control BSA/AML compliance risk; ability to assess BSA/AML compliance risk and facilitate resolution when violations or deficiencies are identified.

Name: Office of Foreign Assets Control Compliance Risk Management
Description: Knowledge of OFAC laws, rules, regulations, and supervisory guidance and the methods to identify, measure, monitor, and control OFAC compliance risk; ability to assess OFAC compliance risk and facilitate resolution when violations or deficiencies are identified.

Name: Commitment to the Rule of Law and the Principles of the American Founding
Description: This core qualification requires a demonstrated knowledge of the American system of government, commitment to uphold the Constitution and the rule of law, and commitment to serve the American people.

Name: Knowledge of the American System of Government
Description: Demonstrates understanding and appreciation of the American system of government, including the Constitution, the Bill of Rights, separation of powers, federalism, and the historical development of the American Nation.

Name: Commitment to the Rule of Law
Description: Upholds the principles of the American Founding, including equality under the law and democratic self-government. Ensures the law is applied fairly and consistently.

Name: Civic-Mindedness
Description: Stays up-to-date on important developments in American government and aligns organizational objectives and practices with presidential and public interests. Demonstrates a commitment to serve the American people.

Name: Driving Efficiency
Description: This core qualification involves the demonstrated ability to strategically and efficiently manage resources, budget effectively, cut wasteful spending, and pursue efficiency through process and technological upgrades.

Name: Fiscal Responsibility
Description: Strategically manages, allocates and monitors financial resources. Aligns priorities and initiatives to justify budget proposals. Monitors expenditures, cuts unnecessary costs, and uses cost-benefit analysis to set priorities.

Name: Managing Resources
Description: Manages resources efficiently and effectively based on current and projected organizational goals, skills, budget considerations, and staffing needs.

Name: Leveraging Technology
Description: Explores emerging technology and potential applications. Incorporates technology to enhance efficiency and achieve results. Ensures access to and security of technology systems.

Name: Merit and Competence
Description: This core qualification involves the demonstrated knowledge, ability and technical competence to effectively and reliably produce work that is of exceptional quality

Name: Technical Skill
Description: Possesses the requisite technical knowledge and subject matter expertise to consistently produce timely, high-quality work. Is considered a strong contributor in his or her domain.

Name: Problem Solving
Description: Engages in critical and data-driven thinking when diagnosing root causes and evaluating options. Identifies and promptly addresses the most pressing, high-priority problems.

Name: Agility and Resilience
Description: Anticipates and adapts to change, new ideas, new information, and new conditions. Is committed to continuous improvement. Deals effectively with pressure and remains optimistic and persistent, even under adversity.

Name: Leading People
Description: This core qualification involves the demonstrated ability to lead and inspire a group toward meeting the organization’s vision, mission, and goals, and to drive a high-performance, high-accountability culture. This includes, when necessary, the ability to lead people through change and to hold individuals accountable.

Name: Accountability
Description: Ensures that employees are appropriately recruited, selected, appraised, trained, and retained. Takes swift action to address performance- or conduct-based deficiencies in employees supervised. Holds self and others accountable for measurable high-quality, timely, and cost-effective results.

Name: Developing Others
Description: Recognizes and rewards outstanding achievement in others. Develops the ability of others to perform and contribute to the organization by providing opportunities to learn through formal and informal methods. Cultivates a dynamic environment in which employees are not afraid to make mistakes.

Name: Executive Judgement
Description: Makes well-reasoned, timely, and effective decisions and considers short- and long-term implications. Communicates effectively with stakeholders across all organizational levels, sharing and guarding information where appropriate.

Name: Achieving Results
Description: This core qualification involves the demonstrated ability to achieve both individual and organizational results, and to align results to stated goals from superiors.

Name: Operational Mindset
Description: Effectively translates strategies into actionable steps and processes. Partners effectively with stakeholders to drive adoption and addresses blockers to ensure successful implementation.

Name: Innovation
Description: Applies creativity to improving products and processes, challenges convention, takes measured risks, and considers ways to simplify and remove unnecessary requirements

Name: Strategic Thinking
Description: Formulates objectives and priorities and implements plans consistent with the long-term interests of the organization by evaluating conditions, resources, capabilities, constraints, and organizational goals and values.
